newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rebounds slightly, eyes on weather.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rebounds slightly, eyes on weather.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures pared gains by Monday midsession on trade and origin sales after they got off to an encouraging start following last week's aggressive sell-off which shaved values by almost one-third in seven days.

The market gapped some $50 higher and made its pre-opening dues before retreating from the day's ceiling on overhead selling. Front-month July gained just $12 at $1,835 by the morning close after a high of $1,875.
September was also up $20 at $1,870 after failing to maintain a foothold above $1,900. It hit a high of $1,910 and a low of $1,865.
But overall volume at 1,870 lots was far from impressive. It included some switch trades notably in July/Sept spread.
Traders said news of a frost-free weekend in Brazil might have weighed on sentiment.
Brazilian cooperative officials and coffee growers in the country's coldest coffee regions said they had not heard of any frosts on coffee farms by 1030 GMT on Monday.
In Guaxupe where temperatures fell to three degress Celsius this morning, any frosts were thought to occured only at lower altitudes and there had been no reports so far of damage to cofffee.
Current low temperatures are due to a polar air mass that has entered the country over land and is expected to keep conditions cold through to Wednesday.
Traders said the sell-off in London over the last week had been overdone and the market was now expected to consolidate at current levels.
"Most of the weak longs had to get out...The market was a bit overdone and we expect some consolidation from here on," said one. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
